cor-dsn-yates.title: Yates’s missing value formula
cor-dsn-yates.html:
In a randomized complete block design with t treatments and b blocks, suppose the observation on treatment i in block j is missing. Let T′ and B′ be the totals of the observed values of treatment i and of block j, and G′ the total of all observed values. The least squares estimate of the missing value is z∗=tT′+bB′−G′(t−1)(b−1).{#eq-dsn-yates}

The iteration of @thm-dsn-missing(c) reduces the error by the factor 1/b+1/t−1/(bt) at every step.

def-dsn-adjusted-means.title: Adjusted treatment means
def-dsn-adjusted-means.html:
For a fixed covariate vector z0∈Rq, the adjusted mean of treatment k at z0 is 𝛄μk+z0⊤γ, the mean response of a unit with covariate z0 under treatment k. Its estimate is 𝛄μ^k(z0)=y¯k−(z¯k−z0)⊤γ^.{#eq-dsn-adjusted-mean}

When no value is named, z0=z¯, the overall mean of the covariates, and μ^k(z¯) is called simply the adjusted mean of treatment k.

def-dsn-bibd.title: Balanced incomplete block design
def-dsn-bibd.html: A balanced incomplete block design (BIBD) with parameters (t,b,r,k,λ) arranges t treatments in b blocks of size k<t, so that each block contains k distinct treatments, each treatment appears in r blocks, and each pair of distinct treatments appears together in exactly λ blocks. Its incidence matrix is the t×b matrix N with nij=1 if treatment i is in block j and 0 otherwise. Treatments are assigned to the units within each block at random, and the labels of treatments and blocks are randomized as well.

def-dsn-latin-square.title: Latin square design
def-dsn-latin-square.html: An a×a Latin square is an arrangement of a symbols in an a×a array such that each symbol occurs exactly once in each row and exactly once in each column. A Latin square design compares a treatments on a2 units classified by two crossed blocking factors with a levels each (rows and columns). The treatment applied to the unit in row i and column j is the symbol in cell (i,j) of a Latin square chosen at random.

def-dsn-rcbd.title: Randomized complete block design
def-dsn-rcbd.html: There are t treatments and b blocks of t units each. In every block, the t treatments are assigned to the t units by a random permutation, chosen uniformly and independently for different blocks. The response of the unit in block j that received treatment i is written yij.

exm-dsn-adhesives.title: Five wood adhesives on six boards
exm-dsn-adhesives.title_html: Five wood adhesives on six boards
exm-dsn-adhesives.html:
In a synthetic experiment, five adhesives are compared for the shear strength of glued joints. Timber varies from board to board, so each of six boards is cut into five strips, assigned to the adhesives by a random permutation. The strengths (MPa) are:

adhesive board 1 board 2 board 3 board 4 board 5 board 6
1 7.89 8.42 8.55 8.30 9.26 9.15
2 8.68 8.69 8.73 8.62 9.72 9.51
3 9.13 9.28 9.81 9.43 10.30 9.41
4 8.48 8.60 8.46 8.95 9.42 9.02
5 8.90 9.17 9.79 9.57 10.24 9.09

The analysis of variance is:

source df sum of squares mean square F
adhesives 4 4.106 1.0266 14.88
boards 5 4.068 0.8136 11.79
error 20 1.380 0.0690
corrected total 29 9.555

The adhesives differ clearly (p=8.6×10−6). The adhesive means are 8.595, 8.992, 9.560, 8.822 and 9.460, and every difference has standard error 2×0.0690/6=0.152. Tukey’s honestly significant difference at level 0.05, q0.05(5,20)0.0690/6, is 0.454 (@thm-mc-tukey applies, with the error mean square of the block analysis, as in @exr-mc-tukey-two-way). It separates adhesives 3 and 5 from adhesives 1, 2 and 4: the significant pairs are 1–3, 1–5, 2–3, 2–5, 3–4 and 4–5. Tukey’s test for nonadditivity gives F=0.07 (p=0.80), so there is no sign that the adhesive differences depend on the strength of the board.

Of 20000 randomizations sampled from the 2.99×1012 possible plans, 1 gave an adhesive F at least as large as 14.88: the randomization p-value is (1+1)/(20000+1)=0.00010, in line with the normal theory.

exm-dsn-adhesives-missing.title: A strip that split
exm-dsn-adhesives-missing.html:
Suppose that in @exm-dsn-adhesives the strip from board 4 for adhesive 2 had split while being cut, so its strength (in fact 8.62) was never measured. The observed totals are T′=45.33 for adhesive 2, B′=36.25 for board 4, and G′=263.95 overall. Yates’s formula gives z∗=5×45.33+6×36.25−263.954×5=9.010. The iteration started from the mean of the observed values, 9.102, gives 9.041, 9.020, 9.013, …. The distance to 9.010 shrinks by the factor 1/6+1/5−1/30=1/3 at each step. Filling the gap with 0 and adding an indicator column gives γ^=−9.010, so the covariate method recovers the same value.

The completed table gives residual sum of squares 1.2788, exactly that of the 29 observed values, but on 19 degrees of freedom: the error mean square is 1.2788/19=0.0673, not 0.0639. Its adhesive sum of squares, 4.0534, exceeds the correct 4.0512 by 0.0022. The correct F is 15.05 on 4 and 19 degrees of freedom; the naive analysis would report 15.85, mostly because of the degrees of freedom.

exm-dsn-reading.title: Two versions of a reading programme
exm-dsn-reading.title_html: Two versions of a reading programme
exm-dsn-reading.html:
In a second synthetic randomized experiment, 48 children with baseline reading fluency between 42 and 118 words per minute are assigned, 24 each, to the current and a new version of a reading programme. The response is the gain in fluency. The new version was designed for weak readers, and the fitted lines of Figure 18.3.1(a) show why that matters. The slope is 0.0156 for the current version and −0.1615 for the new one. The test of parallelism has F=11.2 on 1 and 44 degrees of freedom, p=0.0017. The pooled slope of the parallel lines model would be −0.0638, a compromise that describes neither group.

The estimated lines cross at x=107.7. At a baseline of 60 words per minute the new version adds 8.46 words per minute (standard error 1.56). At 100 it adds 1.37 (standard error 1.46), which is not significant. With c=t44,0.025, the Johnson–Neyman region (@prp-dsn-johnson-neyman) is x<93.5 together with x>152.0. The second part lies far beyond the largest baseline in the data, and it is an artefact of extending two fitted lines. The useful conclusion is that the new version is better for children who start below about 93 words per minute, which covers 33 of the 48 children in the study. With the simultaneous multiplier 2F0.05(2,44), the region shrinks slightly, to x<90.8 (and x>195.6).

exm-dsn-tasting.title: Seven recipes, fourteen tasters
exm-dsn-tasting.html:
In a synthetic tasting experiment, seven recipes of a sports drink are rated on a 0–10 scale by 14 tasters, each of whom can judge only three. The blocks are the lines of two Fano planes, the cyclic sets {0,1,3}+s and {0,1,5}+s modulo 7 for s=0,…,6 (recipes numbered 0,…,6 in this description and 1,…,7 below). This is a BIBD with t=7, b=14, k=3, r=6 and λ=2. There are 42 ratings and 22 error degrees of freedom.

Tasters use the scale very differently: the unadjusted block sum of squares is 69.72 out of a corrected total of 80.71. The raw recipe means, 6.15, 6.10, 5.40, 6.60, 6.30, 6.85 and 6.02, therefore mix recipe quality with the generosity of the tasters each recipe met. The adjusted totals are Q=(−1.30, 0.90, −3.43, 3.13, 0.43, −1.50, 1.77), and the adjusted means y¯+kλtQi are 5.92, 6.40, 5.47, 6.87, 6.30, 5.88 and 6.58. Recipe 6 had the highest raw mean. Its adjusted mean is 6.202+314×(−1.50)=5.88, among the lowest: recipe 6 happened to meet generous tasters, and the adjustment removes 0.97 from its mean.

The adjusted recipe sum of squares is 6.36, and the residual sum of squares is 4.64, so F=6.36/64.64/22=5.03 on 6 and 22 degrees of freedom (p=0.0022). A difference of two recipes has standard error 2×3×0.2108/14=0.301. A complete block design with six tasters tasting all seven recipes, with the same σ2, would give 0.265; the variance ratio is the efficiency factor 7×2/(6×3)=0.7778. A taster judging seven drinks would probably not rate as consistently, though.

exm-dsn-tutoring.title: Four study formats with a pretest
exm-dsn-tutoring.title_html: Four study formats with a pretest
exm-dsn-tutoring.html:
In a synthetic randomized experiment, n=40 students are assigned at random, ten to each of four study formats for an introductory statistics unit. A pretest score x is recorded before the assignment, and the response y is the score on the final examination. The data were generated from a parallel lines model. Randomization balanced the pretest only on average: the four groups have pretest means 62.1, 57.2, 59.9 and 60.5, and final means 72.86, 75.15, 69.09 and 78.09. Figure 18.1.1 shows the data, and the sums of squares and products are:

xx xy yy df
between formats 124.9 −31.4 432.94 3
within formats 3643.9 3159.2 4146.41 36
total 3768.8 3127.8 4579.35 39

Without the covariate, the one-way analysis has error mean square 4146.41/36=115.2 and treatment F=1.25 on 3 and 36 degrees of freedom (p=0.305). There is no evidence that the formats differ.

With the covariate, the within-groups slope is β^=3159.2/3643.9=0.8670 points on the final per point on the pretest. The residual sum of squares falls to SSE=4146.41−2738.94=1407.47 on 35 degrees of freedom, so the error mean square falls from 115.2 to 40.2. The residual standard deviation falls from 10.73 to 6.34. The reduced model, one line for all forty students, has residual sum of squares 4579.35−2595.83=1983.52. The adjusted treatment sum of squares is therefore 1983.52−1407.47=576.05, and F=576.05/31407.47/35=4.77 on 3 and 35 degrees of freedom, with p=0.0068: clear differences between the formats. The test of β=0 has F=68.1. The adjusted treatment sum of squares, 576.05, is even larger than the unadjusted 432.94: format 2 had the weakest students on entry and still finished second, and adjustment gives it credit for that.

exm-dsn-tutoring-adjusted.title: Adjusted means for the four formats
exm-dsn-tutoring-adjusted.title_html: Adjusted means for the four formats
exm-dsn-tutoring-adjusted.html:
In @exm-dsn-tutoring, the overall pretest mean is x¯=59.92. Format 2 had pretest mean 57.2, so its adjusted mean is 75.15−0.8670(57.2−59.92)=75.15+2.36=77.51. The four adjusted means are 70.97, 77.51, 69.11 and 77.59, averaging to the grand mean 73.80, with standard errors 2.02, 2.03, 2.01 and 2.01. These barely differ, because the pretest means are close to x¯ compared with the within-group standard deviation of the pretest, 10.06.

The six pairwise comparisons, with s=6.34 on 35 degrees of freedom, are as follows. The Tukey-type multiplier is q0.05(4,35)/2=2.697, and Scheffé’s is 3F0.05(3,35)=2.936.

formats raw difference adjusted difference se Tukey-type half-width Scheffé half-width
1 − 2 −2.29 −6.54 2.88 7.77 8.46
1 − 3 3.77 1.86 2.85 7.67 8.36
1 − 4 −5.23 −6.62 2.84 7.66 8.34
2 − 3 6.06 8.40 2.85 7.69 8.37
2 − 4 −2.94 −0.08 2.86 7.71 8.39
3 − 4 −9.00 −8.48 2.84 7.65 8.33

Both methods declare formats 2 and 4 better than format 3 and resolve nothing else, although the 2 − 3 comparison clears Scheffé’s bound by only 0.03. Without the covariate the standard error of a difference would be 10.732/10=4.80. The raw difference between formats 3 and 4, −9.00, would then have had a Tukey half-width near 13, and nothing would have been resolved.

Adjustment moved comparisons in both directions: format 2’s advantage over format 1 grew from 2.29 to 6.54, while format 4’s lead over format 3 shrank from 9.00 to 8.48.

exm-dsn-tutoring-slopes.title: Parallelism in the tutoring experiment
exm-dsn-tutoring-slopes.html: For the four formats of @exm-dsn-tutoring, the separate slopes are 0.703, 0.823, 1.035 and 0.992, and their weighted mean is the pooled slope 0.8670. The separate lines model has residual sum of squares 1347.47 on 32 degrees of freedom, against 1407.47 on 35 for parallel lines. The test gives F=0.47 on 3 and 32 degrees of freedom, p=0.70, and the covariance analysis stands.

exm-dsn-typists.title: Keyboard layouts, typists and sessions
exm-dsn-typists.html:
In a synthetic experiment, five typists each type a standard passage in five sessions, comparing five keyboard layouts. Typists differ greatly, and speed rises with practice. A randomized 5×5 Latin square gives each layout once to each typist and once in each session: S1S2S3S4S5typist 123145typist 235421typist 351234typist 442513typist 514352 The analysis of variance of the speeds (words per minute) is:

source df sum of squares mean square F
typists 4 689.2 172.3 82.7
sessions 4 89.8 22.44 10.8
layouts 4 73.6 18.40 8.83
error 12 24.99 2.083
corrected total 24 877.6

The layouts differ (p=0.0015). Their means are 47.06, 50.10, 45.92, 50.30 and 48.94 words per minute, and a difference has standard error 2×2.083/5=0.913.

Had the sessions been ignored, with layouts randomized within typists, the error variance would have been about (MSC+(a−1)MSE)/a (@exr-dsn-latin-efficiency). Relative to the Latin square this is 22.44+4×2.0835×2.083=2.95. Ignoring the typists instead would have cost a factor of 17.35, and no blocking at all a factor of 16.25.

exr-dsn-adjusted-at-zero.title: A2
exr-dsn-adjusted-at-zero.html: Software that fits the model E(y)=μk+βx reports μ^k, the adjusted mean at x0=0. For a pretest scored from 0 to 100, what does this number describe? Show that its standard error can be far larger than that of the adjusted mean at x¯, although both give the same differences.

exr-dsn-adjusted-hand.title: A1
exr-dsn-adjusted-hand.html: From the numbers in @exm-dsn-tutoring, compute the adjusted means of formats 1 and 3 by hand and check them against the values in @exm-dsn-tutoring-adjusted.

exr-dsn-adjusted-ss-formula.title: B2
exr-dsn-adjusted-ss-formula.html: In the one-way layout with one covariate, write Bxx=Txx−Exx, and similarly Bxy and Byy, for the between-groups sums of squares and products. Show that the adjusted treatment sum of squares equals Byy−(Txy2Txx−Exy2Exx), and deduce that it exceeds Byy iff Exy2/Exx>Txy2/Txx. Show that this happens in @exm-dsn-tutoring, and explain it in terms of Bxy.

exr-dsn-band-derivation.title: B3
exr-dsn-band-derivation.html: Prove the claim in item (ii): with c=2Fα(2,n−2g), the band δ^(x)±csv(x) contains δ(x) for all x simultaneously with probability at least 1−α. Is the probability exactly 1−α?

exr-dsn-baseline-change.title: B2
exr-dsn-baseline-change.html: A common alternative to covariance adjustment analyses the change y−x. Show that this is the covariance model with β fixed at 1. Using @prp-dsn-precision’s setting with τ2 the variance of x, find the variance of the difference of mean changes between two groups, and show that it exceeds the variance of the adjusted difference (ignoring the 1/(N−g−2) term) unless β=1.

exr-dsn-best-z0.title: B1
exr-dsn-best-z0.html: Show that ∑knkVar(μ^k(z0)) is minimized over z0 by z0=z¯.

exr-dsn-bibd-connected.title: C1
exr-dsn-bibd-connected.html: For a general incomplete block design with incidence matrix N, replication ri and block sizes kj, show that the information matrix is C=diag(ri)−Ndiag(1/kj)N⊤, that C1=0, and that every treatment contrast is estimable iff rank(C)=t−1. Relate this to the connectedness of @thm-est-connected.

exr-dsn-bibd-eq.title: B3
exr-dsn-bibd-eq.html: Show that EQi=λtk(τi−τ¯) in a BIBD, directly from @eq-dsn-bibd-model and @lem-dsn-bibd.

exr-dsn-bibd-hand.title: A3
exr-dsn-bibd-hand.html: From the numbers in @exm-dsn-tasting, compute the estimate of τ4−τ3 and its standard error, and decide whether recipe 4 is better than recipe 3 at level 0.05, considered alone.

exr-dsn-bibd-params.title: A2
exr-dsn-bibd-params.html: Check the identities of @lem-dsn-bibd for the design of @exm-dsn-tasting. Is there a BIBD with t=7, k=3 and b=7? With t=6, k=3, b=6?

exr-dsn-block-order.title: B1
exr-dsn-block-order.html: The strips cut from a board differ systematically: strips from the outer edge are stronger. How would you modify the design and analysis to remove this source of variation as well? Which design of the next section does your answer lead to?

exr-dsn-constant-covariate.title: A1
exr-dsn-constant-covariate.html: In the one-way layout with one covariate, suppose x is constant within each group. Show that @eq-dsn-ancova-rank fails, and describe the set of least squares estimates of β. Is the adjusted difference of two group means estimable?

exr-dsn-crd-efficiency-proof.title: B3
exr-dsn-crd-efficiency-proof.html: Suppose the block effects are random, βj ∼iid N(0,σβ2), independent of the errors. Show that E(σ^CR2)=σ2+σβ2t(b−1)/(bt−1), and interpret the factor t(b−1)/(bt−1).

exr-dsn-general-var.title: B3
exr-dsn-general-var.html: In the one-way layout with q covariates, use @eq-dsn-ancova-var to show that the adjusted difference 𝛄(y¯k−y¯l)−(z¯k−z¯l)⊤γ^ has variance σ2{1/nk+1/nl+(z¯k−z¯l)⊤Ezz−1(z¯k−z¯l)}.

exr-dsn-graeco.title: B4
exr-dsn-graeco.html: A Graeco-Latin square superimposes two Latin squares of the same order so that every ordered pair of symbols occurs exactly once. Write down one of order 3, state the model with rows, columns and two treatment factors, and give the analysis of variance table with its degrees of freedom. How many error degrees of freedom remain for a=3, 4 and 5?

exr-dsn-interacted.title: C1
exr-dsn-interacted.html: In a two-group randomized experiment, show that the treatment coefficient in the least squares fit of y on 1, T, x−x¯ and T(x−x¯), where x¯ is the overall mean, equals (y¯1−β^1(x¯1−x¯))−(y¯0−β^0(x¯0−x¯)), with β^k the within-group slopes. Compare with the adjusted difference of the parallel lines model.

exr-dsn-inverse-chisq.title: B1
exr-dsn-inverse-chisq.html: Let V∼χ2(ν) with ν>2. Show that E(1/V)=1/(ν−2), and that E(1/V)=∞ for ν≤2.

exr-dsn-jn-bounded.title: B1
exr-dsn-jn-bounded.html: Give a numerical example of two groups for which A<0 and the Johnson–Neyman region of @prp-dsn-johnson-neyman is a bounded interval. Interpret the region.

exr-dsn-latin-count.title: A1
exr-dsn-latin-count.html: Show that the cyclic array k(i,j)=i+jmoda is a Latin square, and that permuting its rows, its columns, or its symbols gives a Latin square. For a=3, how many distinct Latin squares are there, and does the randomization described above reach all of them?

exr-dsn-latin-efficiency.title: B1
exr-dsn-latin-efficiency.html: In a Latin square, suppose the columns had not been used as a blocking factor, so that the treatments were randomized within rows only. Following @prp-dsn-crd-efficiency, show that the expected error mean square of that design is σ2+∑j(κj−κ¯)2/(a−1), and that (MSC+(a−1)MSE)/a is unbiased for it in the Latin square.

exr-dsn-latin-interaction.title: B2
exr-dsn-latin-interaction.html: In a 4×4 Latin square, the row-by-column interaction space of the 16 cells has dimension 9. Show that the treatment space (centred) lies inside it, and that the error space is its orthogonal complement within it, of dimension 6. What does this imply about the effect of a row-by-column interaction on the treatment comparisons?

exr-dsn-latin-missing.title: A3
exr-dsn-latin-missing.html: Derive the analogue of Yates’s formula for one missing value in an a×a Latin square: z∗={a(R′+C′+T′)−2G′}/{(a−1)(a−2)}, where R′, C′ and T′ are the observed totals of the row, column and treatment of the missing cell.

exr-dsn-missing-covariate-se.title: C1
exr-dsn-missing-covariate-se.html: Show that the covariance method of @thm-dsn-missing(d) gives correct standard errors for estimable functions of 𝛃β, without any correction, when the software’s estimated covariance matrix of 𝛃𝛄(β^,γ^) is used. Why does this not contradict the warning at the end of the section?

exr-dsn-missing-rank-fail.title: A2
exr-dsn-missing-rank-fail.html: In a randomized block design with t=3 and b=2, suppose both observations on treatment 1 are lost. Show that @eq-dsn-missing-rank fails, and that Mmm has an eigenvalue equal to 1. What happens to the iteration?

exr-dsn-random-blocks.title: C1
exr-dsn-random-blocks.html: In @eq-dsn-rcbd-model let the block effects be random, βj ∼iid N(0,σβ2), independent of the errors. Show that the treatment means y¯i⋅ are equicorrelated, with variance (σ2+σβ2)/b and covariance σβ2/b, while every contrast estimate keeps the distribution given by @thm-dsn-rcbd(b). Show that E(MSB)=σ2+tσβ2, and that (MSB+(t−1)MSE)/(tb) is unbiased for Var(y¯i⋅). Why is s/b the right scale for comparing treatments but the wrong standard error for a single treatment mean?

exr-dsn-randomization-var.title: B2
exr-dsn-randomization-var.html: In @prp-dsn-randomization, show that Cov(∑iciy¯i⋅,∑idiy¯i⋅)=SW2∑icidi/b for two contrasts. Conclude that orthogonal contrasts are uncorrelated over the randomization, as they are under the normal model.

exr-dsn-rcbd-df.title: A1
exr-dsn-rcbd-df.html: An experiment has t=4 treatments in b=8 blocks. Give the degrees of freedom of the block design’s error, and of the error of a completely randomized design with the same 32 units. How large must the relative efficiency (without Fisher’s factor) be for blocking to be worthwhile?

exr-dsn-rcbd-hand.title: A2
exr-dsn-rcbd-hand.html: Verify from the table in @exm-dsn-adhesives that the treatment mean of adhesive 3 is 9.560, and compute the difference between adhesives 3 and 5 with its standard error. Is it significant by Tukey’s criterion?

exr-dsn-shift-invariance.title: C1
exr-dsn-shift-invariance.html: In the one-way covariance model, show that replacing x by a+cx with c≠0 leaves the fitted values, SSE, the adjusted treatment sum of squares and the adjusted differences unchanged. Then replace x by x+dk on group k, with group-specific constants dk. Show that β^ and SSE are unchanged but the adjusted differences and the adjusted treatment sum of squares change. Explain why a covariate recorded with a group-specific calibration error is dangerous.

exr-dsn-slope-f.title: A2
exr-dsn-slope-f.html: From the numbers in @exm-dsn-tutoring, compute the F statistic for β=0 and check that its square root is the t statistic β^/(s/Exx).

exr-dsn-slopes-crossing.title: A2
exr-dsn-slopes-crossing.html: In @exm-dsn-reading, the estimated lines cross at x=107.7. Explain why the Johnson–Neyman region never contains the crossing point, whatever the multiplier.

exr-dsn-slopes-noncentrality.title: B2
exr-dsn-slopes-noncentrality.html: In the tutoring experiment, suppose the true slopes were 0.8,0.8,0.8,1.2 and σ=6. Using the Exx,k of the example (their sum is 3643.9; take them equal for the calculation), compute the noncentrality of the test of parallelism and its power at level 0.05 (@thm-glh-power).

exr-dsn-tukey-coverage.title: C2
exr-dsn-tukey-coverage.html: For four groups of ten and one covariate, simulate the simultaneous coverage of the Tukey-type intervals of @exm-dsn-tutoring-adjusted when the covariate means are held at (62,57,60,61) and when they are held at (70,50,60,60), with the within-group covariate variation as in the example. How far from 0.95 is the coverage in each case?

exr-dsn-tukey-exact.title: C1
exr-dsn-tukey-exact.html: Suppose all groups have size m and the covariate means z¯1,…,z¯g are equal. Show that the adjusted differences μ^k−μ^l are the raw differences y¯k−y¯l, that these are independent of s2 from the covariance model, and that the Tukey intervals built from s and qα(g,n−g−q) have simultaneous coverage exactly 1−α.

exr-dsn-two-missing.title: B2
exr-dsn-two-missing.html: Suppose two values are missing in a randomized block design, in different treatments and different blocks. Write Mmm explicitly and find its eigenvalues. Check the rate 0.367 quoted for the adhesive experiment.

exr-dsn-two-slopes.title: A1
exr-dsn-two-slopes.html: For g=2, show that @eq-dsn-slopes-ss reduces to SSslopes=Exx,1Exx,2Exx,1+Exx,2(β^1−β^2)2, and that the F statistic is the square of the two-sample t statistic for the difference of slopes.

exr-dsn-yates-bias.title: B1
exr-dsn-yates-bias.html: In the randomized block design with one missing value, show that the treatment sum of squares computed from the completed table exceeds the correct one by {B′−(t−1)z∗}2t(t−1). Check the formula against the numbers in @exm-dsn-adhesives-missing.

exr-dsn-yates-hand.title: A1
exr-dsn-yates-hand.html: Verify the arithmetic of Yates’s formula in @exm-dsn-adhesives-missing, and check that the filled-in value 9.010 makes the residual of that cell in the completed table exactly zero.

lem-dsn-bibd.title: Identities for balanced incomplete block designs
lem-dsn-bibd.title_html: Identities for balanced incomplete block designs
lem-dsn-bibd.html:
For a BIBD:

  1. bk=tr and λ(t−1)=r(k−1);

  2. NN⊤=(r−λ)It+λJt, where Jt=11⊤;

  3. r>λ, and b≥t (Fisher’s inequality).

lem-dsn-srs.title: Sample variance without replacement
lem-dsn-srs.html: Let u1,…,uN be fixed numbers with mean u¯ and S2=∑a(ua−u¯)2/(N−1). If S is a simple random sample of m≥2 of the indices, drawn without replacement, then E∑a∈S(ua−u¯S)2=(m−1)S2, where u¯S is the sample mean.

prp-dsn-adjusted-se.title: Moments of adjusted means
prp-dsn-adjusted-se.html:
In the model @eq-dsn-oneway-ancova with Cov(Y)=σ2I, and for a fixed z0:

  1. y¯1,…,y¯g are uncorrelated with 𝛄γ^, and Var(μ^k(z0))=σ2(1nk+(z¯k−z0)⊤Ezz−1(z¯k−z0));{#eq-dsn-adjusted-var}

  2. for k≠l, Cov(μ^k(z0),μ^l(z0))=σ2(z¯k−z0)⊤Ezz−1(z¯l−z0);

  3. for a contrast ψ=∑kckμk, the estimate 𝛄ψ^=∑kckμ^k(z0)=∑kcky¯k−z¯c⊤γ^, with z¯c=∑kckz¯k, does not depend on z0, and Var(ψ^)=σ2(∑kck2nk+z¯c⊤Ezz−1z¯c);{#eq-dsn-contrast-var}

  4. with z0=z¯, the weighted average of the adjusted means is the grand mean: ∑knkμ^k(z¯)=∑iyi.

prp-dsn-crd-efficiency.title: What a completely randomized design would have given
prp-dsn-crd-efficiency.title_html: What a completely randomized design would have given
prp-dsn-crd-efficiency.html:
Let the N=bt units follow @eq-dsn-rcbd-model, with fixed block effects βj, and write Sβ2=t∑j(βj−β¯)2/(N−1) for the variance of the block effects over the N units.

  1. If instead the treatments were assigned to the same units completely at random, b units each, the within-treatment mean square of the resulting one-way analysis would have expectation σ2+Sβ2, over the errors and the randomization.

  2. In the block design, σ^CR2=(b−1)MSB+b(t−1)MSEbt−1{#eq-dsn-crd-variance}

    is unbiased for σ2+Sβ2.

prp-dsn-johnson-neyman.title: Johnson–Neyman region
prp-dsn-johnson-neyman.html: In the separate lines model with normal errors, let s2=SSEsep/(n−2g) and fix a multiplier c>0. Write Δμ=μ^k−μ^l and Δβ=β^k−β^l. The set of x with |δ^(x)|>csv(x) is {x:Ax2+Bx+C>0}, where A=Δβ2−c2s2(1Exx,k+1Exx,l),B=2ΔμΔβ+2c2s2(x¯kExx,k+x¯lExx,l),C=Δμ2−c2s2(1nk+1nl+x¯k2Exx,k+x¯l2Exx,l). If A>0, which happens iff the t test of βk=βl with multiplier c rejects, the region is the whole line with at most an interval removed: δ is significantly positive on one side and significantly negative on the other. If A<0, the region is a bounded interval or empty. With c=tn−2g,α/2 each point of the region is significant at level α. With c=2Fα(2,n−2g) the statement “δ(x)≠0 for every x in the region” holds with probability at least 1−α.

prp-dsn-precision.title: The precision of adjustment
prp-dsn-precision.html: Consider a one-way layout with g groups of m units, N=gm. Suppose the covariate is measured before randomization, so that the xi are independent N(ξ,τ2) whatever their group, and that given all the x’s the yi are independent and normal, with E(yi∣xi)=μk+βxi for unit i in group k and Var(yi∣xi)=σ2. Let ρ be the within-group correlation of x and y. For two groups k≠l, the unadjusted estimate y¯k−y¯l and the adjusted estimate (y¯k−y¯l)−β^(x¯k−x¯l) are both unbiased for μk−μl. If N−g>2, Var(adjusted)Var(unadjusted)=(1−ρ2)(1+1N−g−2).{#eq-dsn-precision}

prp-dsn-randomization.title: Randomization moments of the block analysis
prp-dsn-randomization.title_html: Randomization moments of the block analysis
prp-dsn-randomization.html:
Let the units of block j have values ξj1,…,ξjt, with mean ξ¯j and Wj=∑s(ξjs−ξ¯j)2, and put SW2=1b(t−1)∑jWj, the average within-block variance of the unit values. Under unit–treatment additivity and the randomization of @def-dsn-rcbd:

  1. every contrast estimate ∑iciy¯i⋅ has randomization mean ∑iciτi and randomization variance SW2∑ici2/b;

  2. E(SSE/((t−1)(b−1)))=SW2;

  3. E(SST/(t−1))=SW2+b∑i(τi−τ¯)2/(t−1).

So the error mean square is unbiased for the variance that the model attributes to σ2, and when the treatments have no effect the treatment and error mean squares have the same expectation.

thm-dsn-ancova.title: Analysis of covariance
thm-dsn-ancova.html:
Assume @eq-dsn-ancova-model and @eq-dsn-ancova-rank. Let MW be the orthogonal projection onto C([X,Z]).

  1. MW=M+(I−M)ZEzz−1Z⊤(I−M), and the two terms are orthogonal projections with orthogonal ranges.

  2. 𝛄γ is estimable, with the unique least squares estimate 𝛄γ^=Ezz−1Ezy.

  3. A function 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β is estimable in @eq-dsn-ancova-model iff it is estimable in the model 𝛃E(Y)=Xβ without covariates. If 𝛌𝛒λ=X⊤ρ, its least squares estimate is 𝛌𝛃𝛒𝛄λ⊤β^=ρ⊤M(y−Zγ^),{#eq-dsn-adjusted-estimate}

    so the fitted design part is 𝛃𝛄Xβ^=M(y−Zγ^): the covariance-adjusted response 𝛄y−Zγ^ analysed by the formulas of the model without covariates.

  4. The residual sum of squares is SSE=Eyy−Ezy⊤Ezz−1Ezy,{#eq-dsn-ancova-sse}

    on n−r−q degrees of freedom.

  5. 𝛄Cov(γ^)=σ2Ezz−1, 𝛌𝛃𝛄𝛒Cov(λ⊤β^,γ^)=−σ2ρ⊤MZEzz−1, and 𝛌𝛃𝛒𝛒𝛒𝛒Var(λ⊤β^)=σ2(ρ⊤Mρ+ρ⊤MZEzz−1Z⊤Mρ).{#eq-dsn-ancova-var}

  6. Let C(X0)⊆C(X) with rank r0<r and projection M0, and define Tzz,Tzy,Tyy as in @eq-dsn-within with M0 in place of M. Then @eq-dsn-ancova-rank holds for X0 as well, and the hypothesis that the design part of the mean lies in C(X0), with 𝛄γ unrestricted, has the adjusted sum of squares SSH=(Tyy−Tzy⊤Tzz−1Tzy)−(Eyy−Ezy⊤Ezz−1Ezy){#eq-dsn-adjusted-ss}

    on r−r0 degrees of freedom. If Y is normal, F=SSH/(r−r0)SSE/(n−r−q)∼F(r−r0,n−r−q,γ), where the noncentrality γ, a scalar not to be confused with the coefficient vector 𝛄γ, is given by σ2γ equal to the squared distance from 𝛃𝛄Xβ+Zγ to C([X0,Z]).

thm-dsn-bibd.title: Intra-block analysis of a balanced incomplete block design
thm-dsn-bibd.title_html: Intra-block analysis of a balanced incomplete block design
thm-dsn-bibd.html:
Assume @eq-dsn-bibd-model for a BIBD, with Cov(Y)=σ2I.

  1. ∑iciτi is estimable iff ∑ici=0. Its least squares estimate and variance are ∑iciτ^i=kλt∑iciQi,Var(∑iciτ^i)=kλtσ2∑ici2.{#eq-dsn-bibd-estimate}

  2. The sum of squares for treatments adjusted for blocks is SST∣B=kλt∑iQi2 on t−1 degrees of freedom. The residual sum of squares is SSE=SStot−SSB−SST∣B, where SSB=∑jBj2/k−(∑jBj)2/(bk) is the unadjusted block sum of squares, on bk−b−t+1 degrees of freedom.

  3. Under normality, F=SST∣B/(t−1)SSE/(bk−b−t+1)∼F(t−1,bk−b−t+1,γ), with γ=λtkσ2∑i(τi−τ¯)2.

  4. A randomized complete block design with r blocks estimates each contrast with variance σ2∑ici2/r. The ratio of that variance to @eq-dsn-bibd-estimate is the efficiency factor E=λtrk=t(k−1)(t−1)k<1.

thm-dsn-latin-square.title: Analysis of the Latin square
thm-dsn-latin-square.html:
Assume @eq-dsn-latin-model with a≥3. Write y¯i⋅, y¯⋅j and y¯(k) for the means of row i, column j and treatment k, each an average of a observations, and y¯ for the grand mean.

  1. The centred row, column and treatment spaces are mutually orthogonal. So I is the sum of five mutually orthogonal projections: onto the mean, rows, columns, treatments (ranks 1,a−1,a−1,a−1) and error (rank (a−1)(a−2)). The corresponding sums of squares are SSR=a∑i(y¯i⋅−y¯)2,SSC=a∑j(y¯⋅j−y¯)2,SST=a∑k(y¯(k)−y¯)2, and SSE=∑i,j(yij−y¯i⋅−y¯⋅j−y¯(k(i,j))+2y¯)2.

  2. Every contrast ∑kckτk is estimable, with least squares estimate ∑kcky¯(k), free of the row and column effects, and variance σ2∑kck2/a.

  3. The treatment F statistic satisfies FT=SST/(a−1)SSE/((a−1)(a−2))∼F(a−1,(a−1)(a−2),γ), with γ=aσ2∑k(τk−τ¯)2.

thm-dsn-missing.title: Missing observations
thm-dsn-missing.html:
Assume @eq-dsn-missing-rank, and let 𝛃β^o be any least squares estimate from the observed data alone, that is, for the model 𝛃E(Yo)=Xoβ. Put 𝛃z∗=Xmβ^o, the fitted values at the missing positions, and for z∈Rm let y(z)=(yoz) be the data completed with z.

  1. (Filling in.) 𝛃β^o is a least squares estimate for the complete data y(z∗), and the residual sum of squares of the complete-data analysis of y(z∗) equals SSEo, the residual sum of squares of the observed data.

  2. (Characterization.) The eigenvalues of Mmm lie in [0,1), and z∗ is the unique solution of z=Mmoyo+Mmmz,{#eq-dsn-fill-equation}

    that is, the unique z that equals its own complete-data fitted value.

  3. (Iteration.) For any starting value z0, the sequence zs+1=Mmoyo+Mmmzs, which fills in the current values, fits the complete-data model and replaces the missing values by their fitted values, converges to z∗. The error zs−z∗ equals Mmms(z0−z∗).

  4. (Covariate method.) For any w∈Rm, the model 𝛃𝛄Ey(w)=Xβ+Dγ has rank r+m. Its least squares fit has 𝛃𝛃Xoβ^=Xoβ^o, 𝛄γ^=w−z∗, and residual sum of squares SSEo, on n−m−r degrees of freedom.

  5. (Tests.) Let C(X0)⊆C(X) with rank(X0,o)=rank(X0). The correct sum of squares for the reduced model is SSE0,o−SSEo, the difference of the residual sums of squares of the two models fitted to the observed data, on r−r0 degrees of freedom, with error degrees of freedom n−m−r. The sum of squares computed from the complete-data formulas applied to y(z∗) is at least as large.

thm-dsn-rcbd.title: Analysis of the randomized complete block design
thm-dsn-rcbd.title_html: Analysis of the randomized complete block design
thm-dsn-rcbd.html:
Assume @eq-dsn-rcbd-model with t,b≥2. Let y¯i⋅, y¯⋅j and y¯⋅⋅ be the treatment, block and grand means.

  1. The sums of squares SST=b∑i(y¯i⋅−y¯⋅⋅)2,SSB=t∑j(y¯⋅j−y¯⋅⋅)2,SSE=∑i,j(yij−y¯i⋅−y¯⋅j+y¯⋅⋅)2 are squared lengths of projections onto mutually orthogonal subspaces of dimensions t−1, b−1 and (t−1)(b−1), and with the correction for the mean they add up to ∑i,jyij2.

  2. A function ∑iciτi is estimable iff ∑ici=0. Its least squares estimate is ∑iciy¯i⋅, and ∑iciy¯i⋅=∑iciτi+∑iciε¯i⋅ identically, whatever the block effects. Its variance is σ2∑ici2/b.

  3. The treatment F statistic satisfies FT=SST/(t−1)SSE/((t−1)(b−1))∼F(t−1,(t−1)(b−1),γ), with γ=bσ2∑i(τi−τ¯)2.

  4. E(SSB/(b−1))=σ2+t∑j(βj−β¯)2/(b−1), and E(SSE/((t−1)(b−1)))=σ2.

thm-dsn-slopes.title: The test of parallel slopes
thm-dsn-slopes.html:
Assume x varies within every group, so that every Exx,k>0, and n>2g.

  1. In the separate lines model, β^k=Exy,k/Exx,k, these estimates are uncorrelated with variances σ2/Exx,k, and the residual sum of squares is SSEsep=∑k(Eyy,k−Exy,k2Exx,k) on n−2g degrees of freedom.

  2. The pooled slope of the parallel lines model is the weighted mean β^=∑kExx,kβ^k/∑kExx,k, and the extra sum of squares for the separate slopes is SSslopes=∑kExx,k(β^k−β^)2=∑kExy,k2Exx,k−Exy2Exx{#eq-dsn-slopes-ss}

    on g−1 degrees of freedom.

  3. If Y is normal, F=SSslopes/(g−1)SSEsep/(n−2g)∼F(g−1,n−2g,γ), with γ=1σ2∑kExx,k(βk−β¯)2, where β¯=∑kExx,kβk/∑kExx,k. The test that rejects for large F is the F test of parallelism.
